**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The document's IP architecture meets (and in places exceeds) our preferred position:

- **Ownership/assignment of Deliverables** — §14.2: Customer owns each Deliverable on creation subject to payment, with a present assignment of all worldwide right, title and interest, equivalent personnel assignments, and further assurances.
- **Vendor pre-existing IP** — §14.3 with the §1.9 "Vendor Technology" and §1.4 "Deliverable" definitions (know-how in unaided memory excluded from Deliverables), which also covers the fallback's generic tools/know-how element.
- **Licence back to embedded Vendor IP** — §13.2: perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify and create derivative works; §13.3 limits revocation; §10.1 confirms survival. Since Customer owns the Deliverables outright, the fallback use/modify/sublicense elements are exceeded.
- **Customer Data** — §14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data with no transfer of rights to Vendor; §15.1 restricts processing to documented instructions and bars sale, advertising use, cross-customer combination and model training.
- **No joint ownership** — §14.4, absent a separately signed instrument that we would have to execute; feedback stays unrestricted for us.

Noted but not flagged: §14.1's processing purposes read "provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer" rather than solely to provide the Services. That is a minor breadth short of preferred wording only — the purposes are tethered to Services for Customer and §15.1 forecloses any resale, advertising, cross-customer or model-training exploitation, so there is no material failure of the fallback and no basis to redline.
